eye.because: W is clearly the earliest. House A has two ordinary windows on its ground floor and house B has narrow trimmed upper windows. In X, Y and Z, A has a blank shopfront board and a sign box in place of those windows, and B's upper windows are wider and plain. I read those as later changes that were not undone. X and Z match each other and differ from W and Y in three ways: D (the house at the top of the lane) has shutters instead of glass, there is a rail or post at the far left edge of A, and the shutter state of D flips. W and Y have glazed D windows and no rail. I take the glazed pair as earlier and the shuttered pair as later, because the rail seems to be something added. That puts Y second, which is fairly sure. I could not tell X from Z at all, so their order is a guess. The years are rough guesses from the window style and the shopfront, since nothing in the scene dates itself.

street.because: The frames split into two pairs. In Y and Z, C (left) has boarded side windows and D (on the rock, right) has glass. In W and X it is the other way round: C is glazed and D is boarded. W and X are identical to me, and so are Y and Z apart from a few board-line and roof-line details. Because the same two house states appear in the eye view with the shopfront house, and that view starts with the glazed-D, boarded-C state, I put the C-boarded pair first and the D-boarded pair last. Within the pairs I guessed from weathering, since Y's board lines look harder than Z's. That is a weak cue. Which pair comes first is a judgement, and the order within each pair is nearly a coin toss.

12m.because: The same two house states show. In W and X, C is boarded and D (the gabled house on the right) has glass. In Y and Z, C is glazed and its roof and siding lines look finer, as if repaired, and D is boarded. D's cladding lines are stronger in Y than in Z, which might mean more neglect, so I put Z before Y. The two states are placed using the eye view, where the C-boarded, D-glazed state goes with the earliest frame. W against X is a guess, since I cannot tell them apart.

city.because: From above, X and Z show C (the house below the middle, with the light roof) with a boarded gable window, D (on the rock, bottom left) glazed, and no railing at A's left corner. W and Y show C glazed, D boarded and a railing at A's left corner. I put the first state earlier, using the eye view. The other differences are too small to rely on. Z has a faint streaky texture on several roofs, which I took as slightly more weathered, so I put Z after X. W against Y I could not separate at all.
